name: Liberia
summary_text: Liberia is dangerous for trans visitors. Sodomy is criminalised (1 year, both sexes — a domestic-origin law, never colonised); a legislator is seeking support for a harsh 2024 anti-homosexuality bill (so far unsuccessful); mob violence is documented; no LGR.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Liberia's criminalisation of same-sex activity (misdemeanour, up to 1 year).

sources.title: Liberia: Legislator seeks supporters for his harsh anti-homosexuality bill
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Oct 2024): Liberian Representative Johnson Williams seeks supporters for a harsh anti-homosexuality bill - raising penalties to 10 years (life for repeat/'aggravated' offences), imprisoning children as young as 10, and outlawing LGBTIQ+ advocacy and 'promotion of homosexuality'; so far he has announced no success attracting supporters.

UNDP/OHCHR 'SOGIR in Africa: Liberia Country Report' (April 2020): participatory review and analysis of the legal, social and human-rights environment for people of diverse sexual orientation and gender identity in Liberia.

sources.title: Liberian LGBT Rights Under Spotlight : NPR
sources.claim_summary: NPR (April 2012): 'Liberian LGBT Rights Under Spotlight' - anti-gay sentiment growing since the US announced plans to promote LGBT rights overseas; new legislation calls for longer jail terms for homosexuality; fliers targeting gay-rights supporters.

sources.title: Nobel peace prize winner defends law criminalising homosexuality in Liberia | Liberia | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (March 2012): Nobel peace prize winner President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf defended Liberia's law criminalising homosexual acts - 'We like ourselves just the way we are' - in a joint interview with a visibly uncomfortable Tony Blair.

Liberia's Decent Work Act 2015 (full text): the country's labour law - fundamental rights at work, employment, institutions; relevant as the statutory framework within which workplace discrimination protections would sit.
